mainEntity.name: How quickly can a broken door window be replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common door panes are frequently available same day or next day. Quarter glass, vent glass and lower-volume models take longer to source. We check availability while you are on the phone rather than after you have booked, and we can come out overnight if the car is sitting open.

mainEntity.name: Will my window still wind up and down properly afterwards?

acceptedAnswer.text: That is what we test before the door card goes back on. The new pane is clipped to the regulator, run through its full travel and checked for binding, crooked travel and noise in the channels. If the regulator or motor was damaged, we tell you then rather than handing back a window that drops the following week.

mainEntity.name: Do I need the same tint as the factory glass?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it matters for two reasons. Visually, a mismatched pane stands out from several metres away. Legally, front side windows in NSW have a minimum light transmission requirement, so fitting a darker privacy pane in a front door can put the car outside it. We match the factory specification for the position the glass is going into.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to drive with a side window missing?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not the offence a damaged windscreen in your line of sight is, but it leaves the cabin open to weather and to anyone walking past, and loose fragments keep moving around while you drive. Cover the opening, keep the trip short, and get the pane replaced.

mainEntity.name: Should I claim on insurance for one side window?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your excess and how your policy defines glass cover, which sometimes extends to all window glass and sometimes only to the windscreen. Break-in damage is usually treated as theft or malicious damage rather than accidental, so report it to police and get an event number. Check your own policy. This is general information, not advice.
